newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatility climbs on rally.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatility climbs on rally.

text.p: Volatilities in major U.S. stock index options moved higher Friday as investors scrambled to buy both calls and puts amid another leg up in share prices, options traders said.
"Right now they're just pumping up the upside calls," said an S&P 500 futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "They just exploded volatility."
"They pumped volatility up at least half a point," he said. "In-the-money Junes are probably 17.7 (volatility) and at-the-money Julys are 19.3-19.4"
At 1100 CDT/1600 GMT, the S&P 500 index was up 8.93 poitns at 892.41 and September S&P 500 futures were ahead 7.90 at 903.
Fair value for September futures was pegged at about 9.80 points over cash, with arbitrage buy programs at about 10.60 over cash and sell programs at 9.00 over.
The S&P 100 index .OEX was up 9.06 at 869.30 and the Dow industrials .DJI were up 65 at around 7,777.
"It's unbelievable," one SPX options trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said, referring to the market's dazzling rally of the last several days.
The Dow, which posted its fifth-straight record close on Thursday, has risen about six percent since the beginning of June, when it stood at about 7,330.
The SPX options trader said volatility in the July, August and September was up and June volatility had held firm with just some time decay coming out of premiums.
The CBOE's volatility index .VIX, priced off certain OEX contracts, was up 1.32 points, or nearly six percent, at 23.38.
"They started bidding stuff up right off the bat," the trader said.
Traders said activity was fairly heavy on the market's rally, with both call and put buyers busy as well as some call sellers in the OEX.
The trader at the CME said one brokerage firm bought around 4,000 September 970 calls and another firm had bought about 1,200 of the July 920s.
He said some of the call buying could be short-covering and that one firm was also selling some puts under the market "which means they don't believe (the rally) is over."
In addition, an institution was buying the December 825/890 put spread.
In the SPX, the trader said a brokerage firm continued to roll some of its sizable June positions out to September.
"People are doing a little put protection, just buying puts outright," he added.
Overall, put volume outpaced call volume in SPX options by 40,006 to 30,552 at 1130 CDT/1630 GMT.
In the OEX, put volume led call volume 61,389 to 55,852.
